summary: The Diesel Engine Flexibility Act amends the Clean Air Act to create a 10-year period of regulatory stability for motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, and their engines. It establishes a safe harbor for certain guidance documents related to diesel exhaust fluid monitoring, inducement strategies, and repair-related overrides, while temporarily blocking the Environmental Protection Agency from issuing stricter emissions regulations.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to protections from new stricter emission standards for 10 years and consideration of operational disruption and costs in future regulations.
affected_groups.group: Owners and operators of motor vehicles and nonroad vehicles

affected_groups.effect: Operate under a 10-year freeze on stricter emission standards, with explicit lead times and harmonization requirements for future rulemakings.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers and dealers of motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, and engines

key_provisions: Establishes a 10-year safe harbor protecting the implementation of specific guidance documents on selective catalytic reduction and diesel exhaust fluid monitoring for motor vehicles and engines.
Prevents the Administrator from issuing or implementing new regulations more stringent than the 2007 and 2010 motor vehicle standards during the 10-year period.
Establishes a 10-year safe harbor for nonroad vehicles and engines complying with Tier 4 standards regarding specific guidance documents, including repair-related overrides.
Prevents the Administrator from issuing or implementing new regulations more stringent than Tier 4 nonroad standards during the 10-year period.
Requires future standards succeeding current ones to apply for at least three model years and take effect at least five years after being promulgated.

Mandates specific economic and operational factors—such as resale value, equipment availability, and downtime costs—be considered when the Administrator creates future standards after the 10-year period.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact financial costs or economic savings associated with implementing the bill.
The source text does not mention specific penalty amounts or enforcement mechanisms outside of existing Clean Air Act provisions.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Diesel Engine Flexibility Act amends the Clean Air Act to create a 10-year period of regulatory stability for motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, and their engines. It establishes a safe harbor for certain guidance documents related to diesel exhaust fluid monitoring, inducement strategies, and repair-related overrides, while temporarily blocking the Environmental Protection Agency from issuing stricter emissions regulations.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes a 10-year regulatory freeze on certain federal emissions standards for on-road and nonroad diesel engines, creating compliance safe harbors based on specific guidance documents and setting mandatory lead times and cost-consideration rules for future vehicle and equipment regulations.
